question: Hayes does 3 loads of laundry a week using a detergent pod for each load.  His detergent pods come 39 to a pack.  How many packs of detergent pods will he need to do a full year of laundry?

student_prefix.content: Hayes does 3 loads of laundry a week using a detergent pod for each load.  His detergent pods come 39 to a pack.  How many packs of detergent pods will he need to do a full year of laundry?

Given:
- Hayes does 3 loads of laundry per week.
- He uses 1 detergent pod per load.
- There are 52 weeks in a year.
- Each pack contains 39 detergent pods.

First, calculate the total number of detergent pods Hayes uses in a year:
\[ \text{Total pods per year} = 3 \text{ pods/week} \times 52 \text{ weeks/year} = 156 \text{ pods/year} \]

Next, determine how many packs of detergent pods Hayes needs:
\[ \text{Packs needed} = \frac{156 \text{ pods}}{39 \text{ pods/pack}} = 4 \text{ packs} \]

Since the number of packs must be a whole number and 156 is exactly divisible by 39, Hayes will need 4 packs of detergent pods to do a full year of laundry.
